turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start there.
"Get this over with." Okay. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Look, your son cheated. Everyone knows it. I'm not wasting my evening on this.

My son does not cheat, and "everyone knows" is not evidence. I'm writing down that you said that, word for word. Either you show me a document right now, or I walk straight upstairs to the principal's office with your own policy in my hand.
You lawyers think you can bully anyone.
This isn't about my job, Hale, it's about yours. Your own procedure, section 4.2, says I get a call before any mark goes in, and I didn't get one. Did you speak to Owen first, yes or no?
Are you going to keep wasting my time?

You've had three chances to answer one question, and you haven't. I'll take that as a no, and I'm writing it down. Unless you put something in front of me, the principal's office is my next stop, today.
